knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

```{r setup2}
dir.create("data/raw", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```


## Purpose
Scrape Red Brick Property Management's 2027-28 student listings. Each listing page has its details as "Label: value" lines, so we pull each label with a regular expression.

## Check permission
```{r robots}
robotstxt::paths_allowed(paths = "/listings/", domain = "redbrickmiami.com")
```

## Collect listing links
```{r links}
rb_index = rvest::read_html("https://redbrickmiami.com/studentrentals/2027-2028-student_rentals/")
rb_links = rb_index |>
  rvest::html_elements("a[href*='/listings/']") |>
  rvest::html_attr("href") |>
  unique()
length(rb_links)
```

## Function to read one listing page
```{r function}
get_redbrick = function(url) {
  txt = rvest::read_html(url) |> rvest::html_text2()
  grab = function(label) {
    stringr::str_match(txt, paste0("(?m)^", label, ":[ \\t]*([^\\r\\n]*)"))[, 2] |>
      stringr::str_trim()
  }
  Sys.sleep(1)
  data.frame(
    link       = url,
    address    = grab("Address"),
    house_name = grab("House Name"),
    price_text = grab("Price"),
    rent_type  = grab("Rent Type"),
    residents  = grab("Number of Residents"),
    bedrooms   = grab("Bedrooms"),
    bathrooms  = grab("Bathrooms")
  )
}

# test on 3 listings first
purrr::map_df(.x = rb_links[1:3], .f = get_redbrick)
```

## Scrape all listings and save the raw data
```{r scrape}
redbrick_raw = purrr::map_df(.x = rb_links, .f = purrr::possibly(get_redbrick, otherwise = NULL)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(company = "Red Brick", scrape_date = Sys.Date())
readr::write_csv(redbrick_raw, "data/redbrick_raw.csv")
```

## Clean
```{r clean}
redbrick_raw |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    price     = readr::parse_number(price_text),
    residents = readr::parse_number(residents),
    bedrooms  = readr::parse_number(bedrooms),
    bathrooms = readr::parse_number(bathrooms)
  ) -> redbrick

nrow(redbrick)
sum(!is.na(redbrick$price))   # how many listings have a price
redbrick |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(price)) |> head(10)
```
